author: Tyler Louder
title: Community supports firefighters battling Qury fire - NewsBreak
text:
By Tyler Louder ,
6 hours ago
RAPID CITY, S.D. (KELO) — As firefighters continue to work the Qury Fire near Custer, the community has been stepping up to show support for the men and women on the frontlines.
Community support has continued to shine all week long, even for residents who were close to the fire.
“I live about a mile from where the fire started and so when it was time to head home it was surreal. You look up and you see the mountain on fire, I can’t help but get emotional, it was super scary. I mean any fire is scary but being so close to town and all the residents was extra scary,” Miners Cup Owner Miranda Boggs said.
Miner’s Cup is one of the restaurants that has been providing free meals. Several churches are providing shelter, and even donations from the community continue to come in.
“We’ve got restaurants, hotels, I mean like I said, just everyday residents are stepping up and really coming together to help this out. Making it a lot easier on these people that have been displaced and have not been at their home or have lost their homes,” Custer Mayor Robert Brown said.
“Just a little way to say thank you. We know that they are working tirelessly to battle this fire to keep people’s homes and property safe. I just have to say thank you and I can’t even imagine what we’d do without them,” Boggs said.
Several other businesses have been providing meals this past week as well as different groups and organizations offering services to help these firefighters.
“Whatever they need, we’ve had people dropping off Gatorades, water, and everything else down here at City Hall. Just the whole community has really come together,” Brown said.
Thursday, we expect to hear from the Incident Commander on efforts to contain the fire.
